- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially >0.6) — model tends to overshoot in bullish sentiment periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is weak or negative (sentiment <0.5) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Lag in price correction: model often lags 1–3 days behind true price movements, especially after sharp spikes.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility and fails to smoothly revert to historical mean in medium-term forecasts.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) and underestimate later (last 5–7 days), especially when sentiment is volatile.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment >0.6, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overconfidence; if sentiment <0.4, increase forecast by 2–5% to compensate for underreaction.
